text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged
WeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans
Invite(x, y) ::: x invites y to their ceremony
WellAttendedWedding(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family
Question: 
Based on the above information, is the following statement true, false, or uncertain? John has a larger family.

Premises:
∀x (WeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are engaged
∀x (Invite(x, y) → WeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others make wedding plans
∀x (WellAttendedWedding(x) → Invite(x, y)) ::: Anyone with a well-attended wedding invites others to come
∀x (LargerFamily(x) → WellAttendedWedding(x) ∨ Invite(x, y)) ::: People with larger families have well-attended weddings or invite others
If(Engaged(john)) then (¬Invite(john, y) ∧ WeddingPlans(john)) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends and makes wedding plans
If(LargerFamily(john)) then (WellAttendedWedding(john) ∨ Invite(john, y)) ::: If John has a larger family, then John has a well-attended wedding or invites friends

Conclusion:
LargerFamily(john)
